title: George Whiting and the mix-up over an early collaborator
summary: Johnson praises Whiting's lyrics ('My Blue Heaven') but says the collaborator he once dreamed of meeting was someone else.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, let's see -- so Andy Razaf and George Whiting -- tell us about your collaboration with them.
Yes, George Whiting -- he was a masterpiece, he was a great lyric writer. Of course, when you write a song like 'My Blue Heaven' you've written something.
And that's what he had written when I had met him.
You told me that when you were a kid, that you just dreamed about collaborating with George Whiting some day; you thought it would never be possible.
No, no -- George Whiting was -- no.
Who was the collaborator, who was the person that you had ...
Wait a minute, it'll come back to me -- it wasn't George now, because I didn't know anybody from Tin Pan Alley at that time.
No, but when you were young, I thought that you had told me that it was George Whiting.
Someone else. Who you ended up collaborating with, and you ended up collaborating up with him.
All right, well, we'll pick it up. We've got lots of time.
